title: Ask Needle/Roulette — Prioritization notes and quick plays
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working synthesis of recent customer signals (support threads, POCs, and account conversations) compiled with two goals: 1) propose low-effort quick plays that remove operational pain for mid-market customers, and 2) surface higher-impact feature asks to inform product/infra grooming. Intention is to iterate rapidly — treat as sketch-notes for PM/Eng pairing.

Data sources reviewed (last 8 weeks):
- Top 12 support threads flagged as 'prod-impact' (accounts a/b/c)
- Quarterly CSM health calls with top 20 usage customers (notes from Nia)
- Two private deployment POCs (regulated-fin and healthtech)
- Field notes: Solutions eng troubleshooting sessions (Luis)
- Telemetry spike logs: repeated 503 fallbacks across medium burst windows

High-level themes (synthesized):
1) Observability gaps that block triage
   - Customers cannot map an individual API request to the serving node/variant and KV cache hit-rate. Blind spots slow down incident RCAs.
   - Requests: per-request route tracing IDs surfaced in logs + a lightweight cache-hit diagnostic endpoint.

2) Degraded UX when capacity falls back
   - Several accounts report opaque fallbacks to smaller model variants (quality regressions) without granular signals. They prefer configurable degrade policies and pre-notifications.

3) Cost and predictability pain for batching/cold-starts
   - Biggest ask from growth-stage startups: predictable per-request millisecond tail and easy prewarm controls for scheduled workloads.

4) Limited admin controls in Console for enterprise tenants
   - Need ability to set per-route token budgets, alerting thresholds, and a simple role to revoke model access for service accounts.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We spent a full afternoon chasing a QoS drop because the cache churned — couldn't tell whether it was cache TTL or a different model version." — AI platform lead, fintech customer
- "When you switch to fallback we see hallucinations spike; we'd rather have a short spike and a clear signal than silent quality changes." — Product manager, legaltech
- "We need a button to prewarm for our nightly batch ingestion; right now it's guessing and costs spike." — CTO, mid-market ecom

Concrete quick plays (low effort; 1–2 wks eng + config):
A. Per-request trace token: add a small header (X-Rw-Trace) returned for each API call that surfaces in Console logs. Drop-in for support teams to map customer requests to infra traces.
   - Hypothesis: reduces time-to-resolve for top 30% of recent incidents.
   - Owner candidate: Luis (SE) + infra oncall.

B. Cache-diagnostic endpoint: ephemeral endpoint that reports last-KV-hit-rate for a model-version+route. Restricted to admin roles.
   - Minimal runtime change; safe default off for hosted plans.

C. Fallback-visibility flag: add a field in the generation response when a fallback occurred (original_model, fallback_model, reason-code).
   - Helps customers roll their own alerting for quality regressions.

Mid-effort feature asks (2–6 sprints):
1) Route-level token budgets + alerting: Console UI and API to set monthly token ceilings per route, with configurable throttles and email/Slack alerts.
   - Impact: high for cost-conscious customers (billing disputes reduced).
   - Linked: JIRA-7894.

2) Prewarm API + scheduled warm windows: an admin API to pre-populate KV caches and spin warm replicas for a route at scheduled times.
   - Two modes: light (KV only) and full (replica prewarm + warm cache).

3) Degradation policy editor: in Console let teams (a) choose fallback model families, (b) enable soft-doors (percent traffic before full fallback), and (c) set notification hooks for fallbacks.

4) Latency-SLA simulator: a small sandbox tool that replays your request mix against different batch sizes / quantization profiles to visualize p50/p95/p99 and estimated $/1M tokens.

Risk flags and customer sensitivity:
- Exposing detailed infra traces increases privacy surface; must limit to tenant-scoped traces and obfuscate user content. Work with security on retention TTLs.
- Prewarm may increase cost; surface clear billing toggles and a per-hour prewarm charge.

Prioritization sketch (impact x effort):
- Quick-high impact: A (trace header), C (fallback-visibility).
- Quick-medium: B (cache diag).
- Mid-high: Route token budgets, Degradation policy editor.
- Mid-medium: Prewarm API, Latency simulator.

Suggested owners and next steps:
1) Ship experiment for A + C as an opt-in feature for top 10 enterprise accounts (1 sprint). Owner: CS + Eng-Infra + Console PM.
2) Small spike for B + Prewarm feasibility (2 wks): infra cost model + security review. Owner: Infra eng + Solutions eng.
3) Product discovery session for Route Budgets / Degradation editor (workshop including SRE, Billing, Console UX). Owner: Product-hosted-api + Customer Success.

Metrics to measure success:
- Median time-to-resolve for flagged incidents (expect -30% with trace header).
- Number of fallback-quality alerts generated (should increase initially).
- Customer satisfaction on post-release surveys for accounts in pilot (CSAT >= 8/10).
- Prewarm adoption rate and incremental cost delta (for billing playbook).

Open questions / discussion points for PM/Eng sync:
- Retention TTL for per-request traces and secure access model?
- Billing cadence for prewarm windows (hourly, daily cap?)
- Visibility level for fallback reasons — full transparency vs. aggregated signals?

Draft messaging for early pilot customers (short):
"We're running a small pilot to give you better visibility when inference falls back or cache behavior changes. You'll get a trace ID for each request and a clear flag in responses when a fallback happens. This helps your teams quickly triage QoS changes and reduces noisy incident rotation. If you want, we can also enable a warm window for scheduled jobs to avoid cold-starts — we'll include an opt-in billing estimate."

Files and tickets to follow up:
- JIRA-7894 (route budgets) — PM backlog
- JIRA-8012 (prewarm spike) — infra spike
- Confluence: "Pilot: trace header + fallback-flag" (link above)

Immediate next actions (this week):
- CS: pick 6 pilot accounts and draft outreach (owner: Maya).
- Eng: quick scoping session for trace header + fallback flag (owner: Devon).
- PM: schedule discovery workshop for route budgets (owner: Priya).

Notes to self:
- Keep the pilot small and instrumented; measure both ROI and support load.
- Emphasize opt-in and tenant-scoped controls to avoid exposing internal infra details.

Revision history:
- 2026-07-11: initial compilation (Maya)
- 2026-07-13: added prewarm spike notes and tickets (Devon)
- 2026-07-14: clarified privacy/retention considerations and owners (Priya)

---
End of note.
